items.text: A repository named secure-build-lab on the lab Git server with two commits.
Four passing tests and an exit code of 0, and you saw a failing test produce exit code 1.
Correct predictions (or at least honest attempts) for the five curl requests.
Five stack detective answers and at least five planted problems found.
A learning log entry for Day 1, pushed.
Two merged PRs, each with a description, and you can name the base, head, and commit ID of each.
A PR template and a CODEOWNERS file in .github/.
An active ruleset on main, and the GH013 rejection that proves it works.
One conflict resolved by hand and one commit reverted.
A Day 2 log entry, merged through a pull request.
git log --oneline -1 on the lab Git server's main matching GitHub's, so tomorrow starts where today ended.
A merged .github/workflows/ci.yml and a green run on main triggered by push.
A red run from your deliberately broken test, with the failed step's log read and understood, and the revert that turned it green.
The protect-main ruleset requiring a status check, and proof (screenshot or the gh pr merge refusal) that a red PR cannot merge.
A reusable workflow node-test.yml called from ci.yml, with the required check updated to node / test.
A validated GitLab-to-Actions translation in ~/scratch/translated.yml (copy it into your log, since the lab box will vanish).
At least five spot-the-bug findings and your three trust sentences, in a Day 3 log entry merged through a PR.
git rev-parse main github/main | cut -c1-7 printing the same ID twice, so tomorrow's clone has all of today.
.semgrep/lab.yml with lab-no-eval and lab-exec-taint, and a results table for all eight sample files, including honest false negatives.
.pre-commit-config.yaml with Gitleaks and Semgrep hooks, and terminal output of both blocking a commit.
The three curl answers from the findings platform, a token minted with review and rules only, and code --list-extensions --show-versions showing the plugin and its version.
A screenshot of the editor's Problems panel on scratch/db.js, showing the masked value, and your filled-in prediction table for the four password values.
Proof that --no-verify bypassed the hook, and the failed CI check plus code scanning annotation that caught it anyway.
The five jq answers for your SARIF file, the JUnit counts, and the broken-rule exit code.
.github/workflows/sast.yml merged, and semgrep (repo rules) added as a required check.
A graded AI review and a completed platform capability matrix.
A Day 4 log entry, merged through a pull request.
A .gitleaks.toml with the lab-synthetic-secret rule and [extend] useDefault = true, and the 1-versus-5 finding counts that prove why both matter.
The git show 4e58b92:.env output from a fresh clone, with one sentence on why revoking is the only real fix.
A hook that blocked a commit, and the --no-verify bypass that shows why the server-side check exists.
A merged secret-scan.yml pull request, and the branch rule that lists secret-scan / gitleaks (pull_request) as a required status check on main.
Vault evidence: KV version 3 after rollback, a 200 on the CI path, and 403s on prod and on write.
A dynamic IAM user created and deleted twice: once by vault lease revoke, once by revoking the job's token.
Spot-the-bug findings split into "a scanner caught it" and "only a human caught it," and a completed rotation drill.
